doc.citation: Le Hérissé, A., Paris, F. & Steemans, P. 2013. Late Ordovician–earliest Silurian palynomorphs from northern Chad and correlation with contemporaneous deposits of southeastern Libya. Bulletin of Geosciences 88(3), 483–504.
doc.comment: The shared Moussegouda cryptospore list and its illustrated sample-level subsets overlap; they must not be counted as independent assemblages. The authors favour latest Hirnantian ages for cores 2–8 but cannot exclude earliest Rhuddanian; spore biostratigraphy alone allows Hirnantian–early Aeronian. Reworking concerns acritarchs and possibly chitinozoans, not explicitly spores. Material includes old SNEAP slides and newly processed samples; Moussegouda was previously studied by Calandra (1964, SNEAP internal report). Although Figure 10 mentions southeastern Libya in its heading, every specimen in its caption is from Moussegouda. No explicit KW-2 spore taxon list or sample-specific spore record is supplied. DOI matches the first page; independent Crossref verification was unavailable.

items.age_basis_detail: Acritarchs and chitinozoans support Hirnantian ages for cores 10–9; chitinozoans support latest Hirnantian, possibly earliest Rhuddanian, for cores 2–8. Cryptospores independently assigned to Sub-zone β of the Imperfectotriletes Interval Biozone, with a maximum range from Hirnantian to early Aeronian and a probable upper limit in the Rhuddanian. No graptolite control is available in Moussegouda.
items.setting_as_reported: late Hirnantian glacio-marine diamictites to silt-dominated sequences suggesting a marginal marine environment
items.notes: The authors report abundant, well-preserved cryptospores and a very similar miospore assemblage in all studied samples, supplying one shared species list rather than a sample-by-species table. The paper analysed 23 Moussegouda samples overall, but does not specify the number contributing to this cryptospore interval. Enclosed cryptospores are highly abundant and Imperfectotriletes numerous; species-specific abundances are not given. L. divellomedia is explicitly absent. Sample-level entries below preserve Figure 10 records and the two trilete occurrences; they overlap this interval. Formation assignments were initially tentative and subsequently reassessed. Reworked acritarchs and possibly chitinozoans occur near the base; no spore reworking is asserted.

items.notes: Palynological processing produced no palynomorphs, hence no spores. Figure 4 shows the core-1 74–79 m interval as barren; the prose describes core 1 as 67–79 m. The overlying sandy interval at 0–65 m was not sampled and is not treated as a spore absence.
